anchors.unattained: - Did not deliver the initial Gantt chart - Failed to update the live Gantt chart by the end of the project
anchors.sufficient: - Delivered the initial Gantt including most key identified tasks in scope - Succeeded in identifying most key task dependencies - Delivered the final Gantt reflecting real project status by the project deadline
anchors.excellence: - Delivered both Gantts successfully as expected in content and timing, with dependencies identified - Correct retrospective analysis of gaps between initial and final Gantt is present - Contingency plan for risk management of critical parts of the project are included in the Gantt (ideally first Gantt) - Live Gantt has been correctly maintained throughout project development

sufficient.text: The initial Gantt was delivered.
The initial Gantt includes most key tasks in scope.
Most key task dependencies are identified.
The final Gantt reflects actual project status.
The final Gantt was delivered by the project deadline.

excellence.text: Both Gantts meet the expected content and timing requirements.
A correct retrospective explains differences between initial and final plans.
Critical project risks have contingency plans represented in the Gantt; record whether they were present initially.
The live Gantt was maintained throughout development.

anchors.unattained: - Information sources used are obsolete, inaccurate or untrustworthy - References used are irrelevant or only lightly related to the statements they support - Reference formatting applies a wrong format or a different style than the one required
anchors.sufficient: - Information used is from trusted, rigorous sources - Sources used are deposited in the repository - Sources used are relevant for the statements they support - Sources are cited following the provided style guide
anchors.excellence: - Reviews or book chapters are generally used to support statements about general context of the disease or topic discussed - Original papers are generally used to support statements about explicit facts and mechanisms that were demonstrated experimentally - Students demonstrate awareness of the difference between primary and secondary literature and select sources according to the type of claim being supported - References are commented, clearly identifying the sources most critical to the topic and those that are simply helpful for expanding the context provided

sufficient.text: Sources are trustworthy, rigorous and sufficiently current for the claims.
References support the statements to which they are attached.
Citations and references follow the supplied style guide.
The sources used are deposited in the repository.

excellence.text: Reviews or book chapters generally support general background claims.
Original research generally supports specific experimentally demonstrated mechanisms or facts.
Source selection demonstrates the distinction between primary and secondary literature.
Reference annotations identify sources critical to the topic.
Annotations distinguish contextual reading from critical evidence.

anchors.unattained: - Key databases for the disease amongst the ones showed in class are not used - Interpretation of the database results is incorrect
anchors.sufficient: - The selected databases help to resolve the intended problem - Interpretation of database findings is correct - Databases are used correctly, identifying relevant candidates with clear rationale
anchors.excellence: - Findings are documented with rationale on why they were chosen instead of others - When multiple database records or candidate results are available, the team selects among them using biologically and technically relevant criteria and documents that choice

sufficient.text: The selected databases are relevant to the biological problem, including relevant key databases taught in class.
Database use correctly identifies relevant candidates with a clear rationale.
Database findings are interpreted correctly.

excellence.text: Selected findings are justified against available alternatives.
Selection among candidate records uses biologically and technically relevant criteria.

anchors.unattained: - Basic biological understanding of the disease is not obtained - The essential concepts of gene, protein, structure and function are unclear, confused or incorrect
anchors.sufficient: - The origin and consequences of the disease are understood - The main genetic, protein-level, structural and functional causes are identified
anchors.excellence: - Relevant regulatory or functional pathways are identified when applicable if they exist, as well as important downstream physiological or systemic processes affected - The clinical consequences of the disease are understood, as well as their human impact

sufficient.text: The disease's origin is explained correctly.
Its main consequences are explained correctly.
Relevant genetic causes are identified correctly.
Relevant protein-level, structural and functional causes are identified and distinguished correctly.

excellence.text: Relevant regulatory or functional pathways are explained (conditional: when applicable).
Important downstream physiological or systemic effects are explained.
Clinical consequences are understood.
The human impact of the disease is understood.

anchors.unattained: - The techniques shown in class are not applied or applied incorrectly - The interpretation of the output of each type of alignment is mistaken or incorrect
anchors.sufficient: - The techniques learned which are relevant to the project topic are applied correctly - The species chosen are justified and useful for the topic of analysis - The output is shared in a clear, understandable format
anchors.excellence: - Strong understanding of the techniques used is displayed - The chosen species for comparison are relevant for comparison - Where applicable and possible, reference and disease-associated human sequences or variants are incorporated into the analysis - The team understands what conclusions can and cannot reasonably be drawn from each analysis performed

sufficient.text: Relevant techniques taught in class are applied correctly.
Species choices are justified and useful for the question.
Analysis outputs are presented clearly and understandably.
Alignment outputs are interpreted correctly.

excellence.text: The work demonstrates strong understanding of the techniques used.
Species selection specifically supports a meaningful biological comparison.
Reference and disease-associated human sequences or variants are incorporated (conditional: where applicable and possible).
Conclusions are justified within the capabilities and limits of each analysis.

anchors.unattained: - The interpretation of structural findings between the reference and disease-associated states is unclear or not understood - Awareness of the differences in structure and function between humans and other species is not obtained or understood - There is no clear rationale of why the structure is impacting the function
anchors.sufficient: - The team understands the observed results and can explain them and their consequences from a structural perspective - Homologs are clearly identified, and the conservation (or loss of conservation) of the key functional domain(s) is understood alongside its consequences
anchors.excellence: - A strong understanding exists of the relevant protein findings across the structural levels applicable to the project (eg sequence, tertiary and quaternary structure)

sufficient.text: Structural findings are explained correctly, including reference/disease-associated comparisons where applicable.
Structural observations are connected to functional consequences with a clear rationale.
Homologs are identified correctly.
Conservation or loss of conservation of relevant functional domains is explained with its consequences.
Relevant human/other-species differences in structure and function are understood.

excellence.text: Findings are reasoned through at the sequence level.
Findings are reasoned through at the tertiary-structure level (conditional: applicable to the project).
Findings are reasoned through at the quaternary-structure level (conditional: applicable to the project).

anchors.unattained: - The team fails to integrate their evidence and information at the disease level with the experimental findings at gene, protein, structure and function level - The team is unable to explain the difference between impact at gene, protein, structure and function level - Each part of the project is generated in a disconnected way, without identifying and integrating all information towards a clear biological understanding of the problem
anchors.sufficient: - The team is able to understand the disease and how it manifests at genetic, protein, structure and functional levels - The awareness on evolutionary differences between species is explained by understanding their similarities at gene, protein and function levels in an integrated way
anchors.excellence: - The team can reason about the biological problem in an integrated way and connect it to the clinical reality of patients - The importance of the findings at molecular level is reasoned through a biological understanding of the problem at different scales

sufficient.text: Disease manifestations are connected across genetic, protein, structural and functional levels.
Evidence and analysis findings form a coherent biological explanation rather than disconnected sections.
Evolutionary similarities and differences are explained through integrated gene, protein and functional reasoning.

excellence.text: Molecular findings are connected explicitly to patients' clinical reality.
The biological significance of findings is reasoned across molecular, organismal and clinical scales.

anchors.unattained: - Report format is not respected - Argumentation is weak or not explained clearly - Concepts explained are not coherent to the topic of the project or excessive unnecessary information is included - No attribution is given to the work of each team member
anchors.sufficient: - Argumentation is clear, concise and relevant to the topic of the project - Good argumental coherence exists across all sections of the report - The required report format is respected - Attribution of each team member to tasks, report sections and decisions is clear
anchors.excellence: - Results and discussion are different and well constructed - Abstract respects length and is concise, informative and representative of the project - All concepts mentioned are correctly cited and explained without unreasonably going beyond the project's topic

sufficient.text: Argumentation is clear.
Writing is concise and relevant, without excessive unnecessary material.
Sections form a coherent argument.
The required report format is respected.
Each member's tasks are attributed clearly.
Each member's report sections and decisions are attributed clearly.

excellence.text: Results and discussion are distinct and well constructed.
The abstract respects its length requirement.
The abstract is concise, informative and representative.
Scientific concepts are correctly cited and explained within the project's scope.

anchors.unattained: - Individual team members show lacking understanding of the content they defend in the written report - Team members fail to explain their findings or statements meaningfully - There is insufficient team member coordination during presentation - Team members show "niche awareness" and only know about the tasks they executed themselves
anchors.sufficient: - All team members show a good understanding of all parts of the project - All claims made in the written report are successfully defended and owned by all team members - Presentation strategy is clear and coordinated - The support used (either existing or not) contributes meaningfully to explaining and defending the project
anchors.excellence: - Team members show excellent preparation, coordination and division of roles according to their strategy - Questions are addressed correctly within the expected level of understanding, concisely and answers distinguish evidence-supported reasoning from unsupported speculation - All team members display excellent understanding of the project as a whole

sufficient.text: Presentation strategy is clear.
Delivery is coordinated across members.
Presentation support, including a deliberate choice not to use aids, contributes meaningfully to the explanation.

excellence.text: The team demonstrates excellent preparation and coordination.
Division of roles serves the presentation strategy effectively.

sufficient.text: The student demonstrates good understanding across all parts of the project, beyond their own tasks.
The student meaningfully explains the findings and statements they present.
The student can defend report claims when asked.

excellence.text: Answers are correct at the expected level.
Answers are concise.
Answers distinguish evidence-supported reasoning from unsupported speculation.
The student demonstrates excellent understanding of the whole project.

anchors.unattained: - Incorrect identification of the problem to be solved - Incorrect splitting of the problems into tasks to be completed - Most tasks are assigned to several or all team members - Project deliverables are submitted without respecting deadlines
anchors.sufficient: - Research problem is correctly identified - Each part of the research problem is split into actionable tasks - Most tasks are assigned fairly across team members - All deliverables are on time
anchors.excellence: - Obstacles are identified early, documented and addressed through appropriate adaptation or previously planned mitigation when available - Most tasks are successfully completed within the team's own planned timelines - Decision-making or complex tasks are performed by several members and operational tasks are done by individuals

sufficient.text: The research problem is identified correctly.
The problem is divided into actionable tasks.
Most tasks are assigned fairly across members.
Deliverables meet their deadlines.

excellence.text: Obstacles are identified early and documented.
Obstacles are addressed through adaptation or planned mitigation.
Most tasks meet the team's planned timelines.
Complex decisions involve several members while operational work has individual ownership.

sufficient.text: The student has clear responsibility for an appropriate share of actionable tasks.
The student fulfils their assigned responsibilities in time for the team's deliverables.

excellence.text: The student's assigned tasks generally meet the team's planned timelines.
The student owns operational work and participates appropriately in collaborative complex decisions.

anchors.unattained: - The project formatting requirements are not respected - Commits are done by a single individual - Commits are done in bulk or at deadlines instead of as continuous progress increments - Contribution of different team members varies greatly
anchors.sufficient: - All team members contribute reasonably to the project progress - Commits are incremental during the project development - The repository is structured and organized cleanly during the entire project development
anchors.excellence: - Commits show clear governance of tasks: operational tasks are performed by individuals and complex tasks receive commits from multiple team members - Commits consistently contain clear, brief comments highlighting the content and rationale of the changes made - The Git history faithfully reflects progressive project development, without substantial work being completed outside version control and subsequently bulk-uploaded

sufficient.text: The repository respects the required project formatting.
Repository structure remains clean and organised throughout development.
History shows incremental progress rather than deadline-only bulk uploads.
Contributions are reasonably distributed across the team.

excellence.text: History shows individual operational ownership and collaboration on complex tasks.
Commit messages clearly and briefly explain content and rationale.
Git history faithfully represents progressive development without substantial off-repository work later bulk-uploaded.

sufficient.text: The student contributes reasonably to project progress.
The student's changes show incremental work throughout their period of involvement.

excellence.text: The student's contributions reflect appropriate task ownership and collaboration.
Their commit messages clearly and briefly explain content and rationale.
Their history represents progressive development rather than substantial off-repository work later bulk-uploaded.
